overall: The AG found that the district attorneys, when meeting at MDAA-facilitated sessions, are not a public body under the Open Meeting Law, so the complaint was resolved with no OML violation; records questions were referred to the Public Records Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the MDAA's board of directors is a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law and sought unredacted agendas and minutes of district attorney meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Following our review, we conclude that the district attorneys, when attending meetings facilitated by the MDAA, do not constitute a public body under the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant also requested the district attorney meeting agendas and minutes through a public records request, which the AG addressed only by referral.
allegations.key_passage: While the district attorneys' meetings are not subject to the Open Meeting Law, records of their meetings may be subject to the Public Records Law.
